column1: # RENAME LEDGER — the rename history the public root cannot carry (127/VERIFICATION F-A).
# The repository was cut to a public root at e4c8824 (2026-09-13); every rename recorded before
# that commit is unreachable from HEAD, and the cited-path resolver (119/ADR-004) answers
# citations "through a rename this repository recorded". This file is that record, DERIVED ONCE
# with the resolver's own argv over the archived history and never hand-edited:
# (1,128 records at b15bb731, 2026-09-16; 0 lines carry a private term.) The line shape is git's
# own `R<score>\t<from>\t<to>`, so `parseRenameRecords` reads it unchanged; lines that do not
# match are ignored. Git's live records are read FIRST (newest first), this ledger after them, so
# a name renamed again after the cut resolves through its most recent life. A rename recorded
# here that git also records is harmless: the first record for a `from` wins.
